author: Trellis contributors
name: Trellis Clean Architecture Solution
description: A rich-DDD, Clean Architecture .NET 10 solution with vertical-slice minimal APIs, separate Infrastructure and Persistence projects, Aspire orchestration and an optional Blazor UI.

IncludeUI.description: Include the Blazor web UI (UI.Common + UI.Web) and wire it into the Aspire AppHost.

skipRestore.description: Skip the automatic 'dotnet restore' after the project is created.

UseRedis.description: Add a Redis distributed cache (HybridCache L2) and wire it into the Aspire AppHost.

UseSerilog.description: Use Serilog for structured logging (console sink) in the API and web hosts, alongside OpenTelemetry.

UseMultitenancy.description: Add a tenant seam: a tenant claim on the principal (ITenantContext), a TenantId shadow column and a "Tenant" EF query filter on every aggregate root. Regenerate the initial migration after enabling.

IncludeUiTests.description: Include a browser-driven UI test project (Playwright). Tests are opt-in at run time via RUN_UI_TESTS=1.

projectPathName.description: File and folder names take the same identifier-safe form the engine writes into file content (acme-shop -> acme_shop). Without it, paths keep the raw name (acme-shop.Api) while the .slnx and every ProjectReference say acme_shop.Api, so the solution does not load. A no-op for dotted PascalCase names (Acme.Shop).

aspireProjectPrefix.description: Aspire generates Projects.<project file name with '.' replaced by '_'>. Without this, a dotted name like Acme.Shop would emit Projects.Acme.Shop_Api, which does not exist; starting from the identifier-safe form keeps kebab-case names (acme-shop -> Projects.acme_shop_Api) valid too.

aspireResourcePrefix.description: Aspire resource names allow only letters, digits and hyphens, so every other character in the project name (dots, underscores, spaces) becomes a hyphen.

envVarPrefix.description: The engine generates no upper-case form of the name, so without this TRELLIS_SDK_IMAGE (scripts/dotnet.sh, scripts/ef.sh) and TRELLIS_DESIGNTIME_DB (AppDbContextFactory) would survive into generated projects. Acme.Shop -> ACME_SHOP_SDK_IMAGE.

nameIsDottedAlphanumeric.description: False for names such as acme-shop, Acme_Shop or '1Shop': the engine writes them as underscored identifiers (acme_shop), which the solution's analyzers reject (CA1707, an error in every configuration). Drives the warning post-action. No 'datatype' on purpose: check-template-toggles.sh treats every "datatype": "bool" symbol as a user-facing toggle.

TemplateSource.description: Always false once the engine runs, so a block conditioned on it survives only in the template's own repository, which nothing ever processes (example: the ci.yml step that runs the maintainer-only check-template-toggles.sh). No 'datatype', for the same reason as nameIsDottedAlphanumeric.

templatePackageId.description: The NuGet package id, written into the .trellis-template.json marker. A constant, so the engine writes it as is: spelled out in the marker it would be renamed with the project like every other occurrence of the template's name.

templateShortName.description: The 'dotnet new' short name, written into the marker (docs/upgrading.md regenerates with it).

templateVersion.description: The template version written into the marker. '0.0.0-source' means installed from a source checkout; packing stamps the package's own version over it (eng/Trellis.TemplatePack, StampTemplateVersion), so a project generated from Trellis.Templates X.Y.Z records X.Y.Z.

templateRepository.description: Where the template's CHANGELOG and releases live, written into the marker for docs/upgrading.md.

templateMarkerFile.description: Shipped prose (the README stub, docs/upgrading.md) names the marker as .trellis\-template.json, a Markdown-escaped hyphen that renders as the plain name in this repository; the engine writes the name back as code. Spelled plainly, the name would be renamed with the project like any other occurrence of the template's name, and the engine skips a replacement whose value equals its token.

projectName.description: The name exactly as given to 'dotnet new -n', written into the marker.

devSigningKey.description: Every generated project gets its own Development JWT signing key in place of the repository's fixed placeholder: 'dev-only-' plus 64 hex characters (two random GUIDs, 244 random bits), so a token minted by one project's dev API is worthless against another's. The prefix says what the value is, and it is also why gitleaks' default rules (which skip values containing common words such as 'dev') pass the file with no allowlist entry; a bare hex value of this length is flagged as generic-api-key. onlyIf limits the replacement to the appsettings value; the placeholder keeps working in the template's own repository, where the engine never runs, and needs no .gitleaks.toml allowlist entry.

appHostHttpPort.description: A free port for the http profile's dashboard in tools/*.AppHost/Properties/launchSettings.json, picked when the project is created so two generated solutions can run side by side (the Aspire starter does the same); the source repository keeps 15171.

appHostHttpsPort.description: A free port for the https profile's dashboard in tools/*.AppHost/Properties/launchSettings.json, picked when the project is created so two generated solutions can run side by side (the Aspire starter does the same); the source repository keeps 17171.

appHostOtlpHttpPort.description: A free port for the http profile's OTLP endpoint in tools/*.AppHost/Properties/launchSettings.json, picked when the project is created so two generated solutions can run side by side (the Aspire starter does the same); the source repository keeps 19171.

appHostResourceHttpPort.description: A free port for the http profile's resource service in tools/*.AppHost/Properties/launchSettings.json, picked when the project is created so two generated solutions can run side by side (the Aspire starter does the same); the source repository keeps 20171.

appHostOtlpHttpsPort.description: A free port for the https profile's OTLP endpoint in tools/*.AppHost/Properties/launchSettings.json, picked when the project is created so two generated solutions can run side by side (the Aspire starter does the same); the source repository keeps 21171.

appHostResourceHttpsPort.description: A free port for the https profile's resource service in tools/*.AppHost/Properties/launchSettings.json, picked when the project is created so two generated solutions can run side by side (the Aspire starter does the same); the source repository keeps 22171.

manualInstructions.text: WARNING: the project name became 'Trellis' in folders and namespaces. Underscores fail analyzer rule CA1707, so this solution will not build. Delete it and re-create it with letters and digits separated by dots (for example Acme.Shop).

postActions.description: Next step without a local .NET SDK

manualInstructions.text: No local .NET SDK? Build the SDK image once (the docker build line is at the top of scripts/dotnet.sh), then run: ./scripts/dotnet.sh test Trellis.slnx
Run it: 'aspire run' (needs the Aspire CLI: dotnet tool install -g Aspire.Cli), or without the CLI: dotnet run --project tools/Trellis.AppHost. Seeded admin: admin@example.com / Admin123!
Multi-tenancy is on: regenerate the initial migration before the first run (docs/development.md, 'Multi-tenancy').
